= Admonitions and Quotations

Each of the five admonition labels opens a single paragraph:

NOTE: A note carries an aside the reader can skip.

TIP: A tip is advice rather than information.

WARNING: A warning is about something that can go wrong.

IMPORTANT: An important point is one that is easy to miss.

CAUTION: A caution asks for care rather than alarm.

The label has to match exactly, so NOTES: this line is ordinary prose, and so
is this one, which merely mentions NOTE: in passing.

Admonitions carry inline content like anything else:

TIP: Run `make test` before you push, and read
link:https://example.com/ci[the CI logs] when it fails.

Quotations are prefixed line by line:

> The best way to have a good idea is to have a lot of ideas.
> Most of them will be wrong.

A bare marker separates one paragraph of a quotation from the next:

> First, the claim.
>
> Then, the qualification that makes it survivable.
